correctness.rationale: Exact source coefficient substitution yields the sector law dot(rho)=-2 lambda a (rho-1). On a vertex ray the Filippov tangency constraint uniquely determines convex weight q and the sliding ODE dot(z)=-lambda b²z-omega²/(lambda z). The piecewise-linear gauge of any absolutely continuous solution has the sign-definite derivative at almost every time. Gronwall gives a complete quantified uniform estimate and rules out other nonzero periodic orbits. Solving the square-distance ODE gives the exact residence time; unbounded outer-ray starts prove optimality via the initial logarithmic slope. The standalone checker runs 57 exact/diagnostic checks but is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The main mathematical claim is not mere existence or uniqueness of the polygonal cycle (already studied by Kai and Masuda). The 2026 parent article makes a one-sided transversal hybrid choice, whereas this result treats all Filippov trajectories of its regular-polygon coefficients, including attractive ray sliding. Exact ray normal forms give a globally valid sharp prefactor-one rate and residence time not implied by sector dissipation or other global stability synthesis results. A substantial residual priority risk persists because the 2011/12 predecessors were not fully accessible.

value.rationale: The natural ambiguity in boundary evolution for designed polygonal oscillators creates physically meaningful Filippov sliding not described by transversal hybrid cycles. The theorem classifies global attraction from every nonzero initial point, computes a sharp universally valid rate independent of omega except for the sliding correction, and exactly resolves how long large excursions stick on switching rays. This is a structural and quantitative answer to a precise stability gap, rather than a local textbook deduction or arbitrary parameter slice.
